title: The gate had no way out, and the test suite lied about why it failed
lede: This round started as a plain design review — judge the site the way a recruiter actually would — and turned up two different kinds of problem: one in the gate screen itself, and two in the test suite that's supposed to catch exactly this sort of thing. I fixed all three, then proved each fix with a check that would have failed before it, not just a check that passes now.
meta: UI review + code review + local server
Verified with: a direct fault-injection check, the full 48-test suite, a manual Chrome walkthrough on both localhost and the live site
tiles: a skip link that needed no company name
a state leak and a fragile startup check
verified clean, then verified the new failure path on purpose
Bugs found on the live site
images, console and network all came back clean

findings.title: A recruiter who didn't want to play along could never reach the CV
findings.trigger: Walking through the site cold, the way a recruiter skimming 200 applications would
findings.before: The only way past the gate was typing a company name and waiting through the boot animation — nothing, not even the CV download, was reachable before that
findings.after: A quiet "Skip — just show me the CV" link next to the existing report link submits an empty visitor name through the same /api/gate path the form already used, landing straight on the dashboard with Download Full CV visible
findings.cause: The gate was designed around the chatbot persona first and the plain-CV path was never added as a fallback
findings.fix: Refactored the form's submit handler into a shared enterWith() function and called it from both the form and the new skip link, so the skip path gets identical session handling, error handling and boot sequence — no second code path to drift out of sync

findings.title: One test silently poisoned every test that ran after it
findings.trigger: Re-reading tests/test_app.py cold, checking every test that mutates shared state for a matching restore
findings.before: test_config_put_validation set the site title to a throwaway value and never restored it — no try/finally, unlike test_maintenance_mode right next to it, which does restore its state
findings.after: The mutation and all its assertions are now wrapped in try/finally, so the real title is restored even if an assertion in between fails
findings.cause: The test was written by copying the request/assert pattern from elsewhere in the file, but not the teardown pattern
findings.fix: Wrapped the body in try/finally, matching the pattern test_maintenance_mode already used a few tests earlier in the same file

findings.title: A stuck process produced 28 confusing failures instead of one clear one
findings.trigger: This is the exact failure I hit two sessions ago: a day-old orphaned server from an earlier debugging session was still holding port 8765, and the whole suite failed with opaque connection errors
findings.before: The startup loop retried for 10 seconds and then silently fell through with no assertion — every test afterward failed with its own ConnectionError, none of them pointing at the real cause
findings.after: The loop now raises one clear RuntimeError naming the port and suggesting `lsof -i :8765` if the server never comes up
findings.cause: The loop was written to retry, but nobody added the "and if it never works, say so clearly" case
findings.fix: Added a flag set only on a successful request inside the loop, and one explicit raise after it if that flag was never set — proved it by occupying port 8765 on purpose and confirming the new message fires instead of the old pile of ConnectionErrors

strengths.title: The responsive CSS and the self-test page held up under a second, cold look
strengths.body: Re-checking the CSS without the context of having written it, the mobile breakpoint, touch-target sizing and prefers-reduced-motion handling all still held up fine.

strengths.title: The live site matched the local one, Round 3's Projects fix included
strengths.body: Network inspection of www.adem.ben-halima.com showed every request — including both project cover images — returning 200. An earlier screenshot that looked like broken images was a timing artifact of screenshotting before the images decoded, not a real bug.

checks.name: Gate skip link, manual check in Chrome
checks.detail: lands on the dashboard with no company typed; Download Full CV is visible immediately; confirmed with a hard reload after a stale browser cache initially hid the change

checks.name: Fault-injection check: port 8765 pre-occupied on purpose
checks.detail: produces exactly one RuntimeError naming the port, instead of the 28 opaque ConnectionErrors this failure mode used to cause

checks.name: Live site (www.adem.ben-halima.com), manual check
checks.detail: console clean, all 20 network requests 200 including both project images; gate is skipped on this browser because a session cookie from an earlier visit already exists — expected, not a bug

also: Read tests/test_app.py cold, the way someone unfamiliar with it would, checking every state-mutating test for a matching teardown — that's what caught the state leak above.
method: Reviewed the live gate flow as a recruiter would experience it, cold, before looking at any code.
Re-read the test file cold, checking every state-mutating test for a matching restore, the same discipline test_maintenance_mode already followed.

Fixed the gate, the state leak, and the fragile startup check; wrote a fault-injection check that occupies the test server's port on purpose, to prove the new error path actually fires rather than just assuming it would.
Ran the full suite clean, then re-ran it with the port blocked to confirm both the before and after behaviour.
Checked the live production site's network requests and console directly rather than trusting a screenshot that looked wrong.
